hypothesis: Concealed intrabasin faults hosting blind Great Basin geothermal systems are under-represented in the USGS/INGENIOUS Quaternary catalogue (which favours surface-rupturing traces). A concealed fault cutting Quaternary volcanic cover should co-locate with Quaternary volcanic vents/flows (heat source), paleogeothermal sinter/tufa springs (fluid discharge), and shallow 2 m temperature probes (near-surface thermal anomaly), gently boosted near (not on) SGMC-mapped structure for step-over/splay strands, and gated more than 2 px off mapped structure so dots target catalogue-missing faults without paying the unmasked 1-2 px flank halo penalty.
mechanism: Weighted linear pool of exp(-distance/1000 m) proximity surfaces: GDR Quaternary volcanics (0.4), GDR paleogeothermal springs (0.3), GDR 2 m temperature probes (0.3), multiplied by (0.75 + 0.25 x SGMC-proximity decay); normalized to [0,1]; domain = template footprint minus pixels within 2 px of SGMC mapped structure, belief > 0.10; Poisson-disk thinning at 3.0 px (300 m kernel scale) in descending belief order, capped at 40,000 dots; binary {0,1} emission written with gemsdoe30.submission.write_submission_file as single-band float32 GeoTIFF, NaN outside the template footprint. Builder: scripts/build_geothermal_corridor_submission.py.
non_fault_mimic: Non-tectonic volcanic centers/caldera rings, paleospring clusters and shallow thermal anomalies with no Quaternary fault control (e.g., volcanic geothermal circulation unrelated to a mappable fault trace) can mimic a corridor signal.
